generation.forced_text:
I remember this little alley that led me from where we were living in our tiny, cluttered, one room walkup, to what felt like a bustling street of endless possibilities in a different city block, but the way the world opened out in that narrow pass was something of an everyday wonder.

Every evening after supper and the evening cleaning and tidys were finished up (a nightly chore, the way my family and all our board members had lived), we were allowed an afternoon out on our street and then back home, through that alleyway. I always walked, and usually, my grandmother and father followed along. We would pass under our fire exit that hung open and then into a world of cobalt shadows.

There, a few blocks to the northeast from the back alley where I lived on 8th Avenue with the old, worn down brick houses
